candidates.one_line_claim: R-8 declares dependency-semantics.json as its state authority and R-9 declares fizzy-plan.json, but E-25 places both authorities inside one leaf because they run in the same planning pass.

R-3 assigns the canonical obligation-hash projection and verification to the compiler, although these are keystone §2b contract semantics implemented by tmr_schema and E-1 explicitly makes compilation a contract consumer.

E-11 separates accounting failures from removal-preview failures, but incorrectly calls the preview an effect authority even though R-11 explicitly produces only a verdict and destructive execution is outside scope.

E-12 names the stateless comparator as producer and owner of partial receipts, although R-5 assigns receipt authority to the runner and TC-14.1 requires reconciliation after that runner dies before writing a receipt.
The harness consumes the policy-owned reject-code enum to measure catalog coverage; E-16 reverses that data flow by making the policy consume harness data.

candidates.one_line_claim: Finalize must consult census-owned authority roles for active-versus-legacy classification, but no census-to-finalize edge or interface exists.
The runner produces the versioned CodeRunEvidence observation payload, but the schema contract reaches only its promotion consumer and omits the runner that must emit it.
The roadmap explicitly makes validate_authority_paths consume the shared reject catalog, but its independently owned catalog dependency is absent from the graph.
R-11 emits the shared CUSTODY_DESTRUCTIVE_PREVIEW_INCOMPLETE code, but only the ledger receives the catalog and its interface to reconciliation carries rows rather than policy definitions.
Golden replay must execute ASP-HARDEN-002 against the finalize-owned assertion-versus-schema validator, but the harness has no interface to that leaf.
The fence consumes Fizzy card created_at and pipeline_version, but X-FIZZY names only the plan leaf as owner and attaches a discriminator-parity test that never checks this metadata transfer.

candidates.one_line_claim: R-8's schedule postcondition needs actual materialized readiness from Fizzy, but the external contract provides no return interface for that scheduler-owned state.
Reconciliation must discover surviving host workspaces that have no ledger row, but its interfaces supply only ledger rows and receipts while X-HOST is assigned solely to observation capture.

Projected-budget admission must gate resource creation before the host effect, including concurrent requests, but R-10 starts with an already-created resource and no admission-to-creation control interface exists.
TC-10.2 checks code-name coverage in the catalog without exercising promotion, so it remains green if promotion ignores the policy-provided fence or freshness window.
TC-7.0 supplies a budget directly and tests worktree dispositions without consuming planning output, so it cannot detect dropped or corrupted plan-produced budgets and expected custody rows.
TC-8.2 tests critic output and the next debate round without invoking finalize, so it cannot fail when concern findings or dispositions are lost at the finalize interface.
TC-8.1 supplies an observation and a cross-path request without producing or consuming a census, so it cannot detect a missing census or corrupted census delivery to seats.
